Q1: Antimony exhibits several known hazards (Tier 1) according to the Globally Harmonized System, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, or reproductive toxicity, environmental concerns, oral toxicity, and organ/systemic effects. It also presents potential inhalation and dermal/eye hazards based on expanded scientific data (Tier 2), though information regarding its endocrine disruption potential is currently data deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Antimony is identified on lists of concern, specifically the EPA's Drinking Water Standard, which outlines regulations and health advisories for contaminants in drinking water. There are no listed low-hazard designations for this chemical.
Q3: Antimony is exceptionally well-characterized, evidenced by its 119,000 scientific literature references, which is significantly higher than the median for our dataset of fracking and petrochemical materials. Its molecular formula (Sb) and substance class (Element) are precisely defined, and it is not categorized as an undefined UVCB substance. Furthermore, only one of its hazard classes, endocrine disruption, is considered data deficient (Tier 4).
